correctness.rationale: Exact one-bridge expectation formulas separate clique and star. Star leaves and unmarked clique vertices are strictly dominated; a two-hop lower bound forces the reversal for every integer q≥4, while endpoint limits force center optimality. The nine-vertex reliability polynomial is independently derived by conditioning, transformed Descartes polynomial has exactly two sign changes and opposite signs at three interior boundaries, proving two and only two roots. Accompanying standard-library verifier enumerates all 2^11 edge states and passes 68 exact checks; finite computation is corroboration, not the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The known clique two-terminal reliability and epidemic influence objective are not presented as new. The novel assessed claim is explicit strict global seed re-entry for every balanced clique–star bridge and the exact two-switch phase diagram for its sharp nine-vertex member. Accessible original primary articles and semantic mathematical-record statements have been compared by implication; none of those inspected contains this classification, subject to the named inaccessible-source priority risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Šikić et al. (2013), a conceptually related epidemic-centrality work, could not be accessed; an unrecognized stronger comparison remains possible.

value.rationale: Core–periphery influence optimization has a natural nontrivial choice between a high-degree star and a nearly equally connected dense clique gateway. The exact global optimizer re-enters the star at high transmission despite a middle regime favoring the lower-degree gateway. This holds for all sizes of an infinite family, the sharp family cutoff is proved, and the first nine-vertex instance is fully solved with algebraic thresholds; it provides a reproducible non-degree-monotone benchmark rather than a routine isolated numeric calculation.
